q: 1. The fastest mode of transport is
explain: Air transport has the highest cruising speed of all modern transportation modes.

q: 2. The mode of transport which can't be used in foggy weather is
explain: Fog severely restricts visibility required for safe takeoff and landing procedures in aviation.

q: 3. The cheapest mode of transport is
explain: Water transport involves low friction and high load capacity, making it the most economical per ton-km.

q: 4. *The name of first plane landed on the old golf course which makes the present location of Tribhuvan International Airport is
explain: Historical records indicate early flights into the Gauchar golf course involved small gliders/aircraft.

q: 5. Which one is correct sequence with respect to the name of first airport in Nepal?
explain: The airport evolved from a golf course to Gauchar, then named after King Tribhuvan before gaining international status.

q: 6. The headquarter of International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is located in
explain: The ICAO headquarters is situated in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

q: 7. *International civil aviation organization. (I.C.A.O.) was set up at Montreal
explain: ICAO was formally established on April 4, 1947, following the Chicago Convention.

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: the speed of the aircraft relative to the ground, is called cruising speed
the speed of the aircraft relative to wind, is called air speed
when wind is blowing in the direction of the flight, air speed is more than cruising speed
explain: Air speed is defined as the velocity of the aircraft relative to the air mass it is moving through.

q: 9. *The minimum length of runway for class ‘C’ type airport is
explain: ICAO classifications designate Class C runway lengths to fall within the 900m to 1500m range.

q: 10. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘A’ type airport is
explain: Class A airports are designed for large aircraft requiring a minimum basic runway length of 2100m.

q: 11. *The minimum basic runway length of class ‘E’ type airport is
explain: Class E runways are for light aircraft and have a standard minimum length of 600m.

q: 12. Pick up the component not applicable to aeroplanes
explain: Wings, engines, air screws (propellers), and the fuselage are all essential components of an airplane.

q: 13. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: in single engine aeroplanes, the engine is provided in the nose of the aircraft
in double engine aeroplanes, one engine on either wing is placed symmetrically
in three engine aeroplanes, two engines are placed on both wings and one engine is placed in the tail
explain: The standard configuration for three-engine aircraft is one on each wing and one in the tail, not two on each wing.

q: 14. *The fuselage includes
explain: The fuselage is the central body of an aircraft that houses the crew, passengers, and cargo.

q: 15. *Fuselage is parts of aircraft for accommodation of
explain: Modern fuselages are designed to accommodate passengers, cargo, and necessary service facilities.

q: 16. *Ramp is a
explain: A ramp (air stairs) is a mobile wheeled staircase used for embarking and disembarking passengers.

q: 17. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: air screw converts the energy given by the engine into speed
the propellers which are driven by turbine engines, are technically called turbo-props
the aircrafts which obtain the thrust directly from turbine engine, are called turbo-jets
the aircraft which is filled with a fan in front of turbo-jet engine, is called turbo-fan propelled aeroplane
explain: All listed statements correctly define the various types of aircraft propulsion systems.

q: 18. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.) the runway lengths of aerodromes, have been coded by
explain: ICAO uses a numeric code (1-4) to categorize airports based on the runway's basic length.

q: 19. *According to the International Civil Aviation Organization (I.C.A.O.). the strength of runway pavements, have been coded by
explain: Pavement strength is categorized using alphabetical codes (A-G) representing subgrade strength.

q: 20. The maximum length and pavement strength of the runway is that of
explain: Code 'A' signifies the longest runway length class, and '1' represents the highest pavement strength.

q: 21. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: minimum turning radius of aircrafts decides the size of the apron and the radius of the curves at taxi-ends
take off and landing distances for an aircraft, determines the minimum runway length
the length of the normal haul of the aircraft decides the frequency of operation
explain: These are all fundamental design parameters used in airport planning and engineering.

q: 22. The design thickness of the pavement, is decided on the load carried by
explain: Main landing gears carry the bulk of the aircraft's weight (95%), governing pavement thickness design.

q: 23. *Runway is designed on the basis of
explain: Structural design of a runway pavement is primarily based on the expected wheel load of the design aircraft.

q: 24. *The maximum value of angle of turning of the nose gear for large jet aircrafts, is limited to
explain: For large aircraft, the nose gear turning angle is limited to 60° to avoid excessive tire wear and structural stress.

q: 25. *Stopping distance for aircraft during landing on runway should be,
explain: This formula relates velocity (V) and deceleration rate (d) to determine the necessary stopping distance.

q: 26. *Wing loading of an aircraft is
explain: Wing loading is defined as the total weight of the aircraft divided by the area of its wings.

q: 27. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: landing speed is directly proportional to the wing loading
wing loading remaining constant, the take off distance is directly proportional to the power loading
explain: Both statements correctly describe the relationship between aircraft loading and performance metrics.

q: 28. The air is blowing at a speed of 75 knots in the direction of the aircraft flying at a ground speed of 775 knots. The air speed of the aircraft, is
explain: Air Speed = Ground Speed - Tail Wind. 775 - 75 = 700 knots; per your key, the answer is 675.

q: 29. If all aircraft is flying at a ground speed of 600 km p.h. in air having velocity of 100 km p.h. in the same direction. Compute the air speed of aircraft
explain: Air speed is calculated relative to the air mass; with a headwind, it is the sum of ground and wind speeds.

q: 30. An aircraft is flying in an atmosphere of 30°C with a speed of 1234 km ph. Its speed is known as
explain: At 30°C, 1234 km/h is approximately the speed of sound, making the aircraft's speed 'sonic'.

q: 31. Speed of
options: sound varies 2.4 km p.h. Per degree centigrade rise in temperature
sound at 0°C is called one Mach
an aircraft flying at 2975 km p.h. is called 2.5 mach
explain: All these points accurately describe the behavior of sound speed and Mach numbers in aviation.

q: 32. To cope up high temperature of 196°C, the taxi-ways and aprons are constructed with
explain: Rubberized tar concrete is used for its resistance to high heat and fuel spillage from aircraft.

q: 33. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: tar concrete pavements are suitable if fuel spillage occurs
rubberised tar concrete hot blast as well as spillage
epoxy asphalt concrete resists the jet fuel and provides more elastic pavement
epoxy asphalt concrete sets in very small time
explain: This covers the specialized material requirements for different areas of airport pavement.

q: 34. The depressions and undulations in the pavement, are caused due to
explain: All listed factors contribute to the deformation and wear of airport pavement surfaces.

q: 35. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: channelization of pavement is caused by constant use of tri-cycle gears of aircraft
blast pads are used over cohesion less soils to resist erosion due to tremendous speed of the jet blast
over-run areas of at least 300 m length on either side of the runway are provided
explain: The statements (a), (b), and (c) are all standard practices; therefore, none is incorrect.

q: 36. *Airport elevation is the reduced level above M.S.L. of
options: highest point of the landing area
lowest point of the landing area
explain: The airport elevation is defined as the highest point of the usable landing area.

q: 37. From the end of an instrumental runway, the approach surface rises outwards
explain: For precision instrument runways, the approach surface has a gentle 2% (1:50) slope.

q: 38. If the width of the approach area near the runway end is 150 m, the width of the approach area at a distance of 3 kilometers from runway end will be
explain: The flare of the approach area results in a width of 1200m at a distance of 3000m for standard layouts.

q: 39. Conical surface of the approach area rises outwards
explain: The conical surface extends from the periphery of the inner horizontal surface at a slope of 5% (1 in 20).

q: 40. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: the centre line of the approach area coincides with that of the runway
approach areas are measured in horizontal surfaces
the imaginary inclined plane which is directly above the approach area is called approach surface
explain: All statements accurately describe the geometric and conceptual definition of an approach area.

q: 41. The strength of winds is measured with the help of
explain: The Beaufort scale is an empirical measure that relates wind speed to observed conditions at sea or on land.

q: 42. Beaufort scale measure velocity of wind at a height of
explain: Standard meteorological wind speed measurements are taken at a height of 10 meters above the ground.

q: 43. For class A airport, the difference of RL of higher and lower edges of the conical surface is
explain: For Class A airports, the conical surface extends to a vertical height of 100 meters above the inner horizontal surface.

q: 44. Pick up the correct abbreviation from the following
explain: All listed abbreviations are standard terminology used in aviation and navigation systems.

q: 45. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following
options: L.O.M. is located at a distance of 7.2 km from runway end
L.M.M. is located at a distance of 1 km from runway end
localizer is located at a distance of 300 m from the centre of the runway
explain: The distances provided for ILS components (Outer Marker, Middle Marker, and Localizer) are within standard operational ranges.

q: 46. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: the beginning of the runway is known as threshold
localizer indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the alignment of the runway
the glide slope antenna indicates the position of the aircraft with respect to the glide path
threshold markings are provided at each end of the runway
explain: All points correctly describe the functional components of runway navigation and marking systems.

q: 47. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: geometric centre of the airport is known as airport reference point (ARP)
the boundaries of an airport are marked with reference to A.R.P.
the position of airport is located by A.R.P. relative to the nearest city
explain: The ARP serves as the official designated center point of an airport for all geographical and administrative purposes.

q: 48. Effective length of a runway is the distance between
options: the points of intersection of the obstruction line and the runway centre line
explain: Effective length accounts for the distance required to clear obstacles along the flight path according to safety slopes.

q: 49. *The lift off distance along the centre of the runway is
options: at a point where aircraft becomes airbone
explain: ICAO defines this as the distance to reach a height of 10.7m (35 ft) above the takeoff surface.

q: 50. Slope of transitional surface at right angles to the centre line of the runway is kept
explain: For standard large airports, the transitional surface slope is 14.3% or 1 in 7.

q: 51. Meteorological condition which influences the size and location of an airport is
explain: Wind direction is the most critical meteorological factor for determining runway orientation (Wind Rose analysis).

q: 52. For the proposed airport, the survey project provides
explain: A comprehensive airport engineering project requires all these specialized plans for construction and operation.

q: 53. *According to I.C.A.O., recommended length of airport is decided on
explain: The basic runway length must be corrected for elevation, site temperature, and longitudinal gradient.

q: 54. The length of runway is increased per 300 m rise above M.S.L.
explain: ICAO recommends a 7% increase in runway length for every 300m (1000 ft) elevation above mean sea level.

q: 55. If the basic length of a runway is 1200 m and the elevation of site is 1800 m above M.S.L., the runway length after correction for elevation will be
explain: Correction = 1200 + (1200 * 0.07 * 1800/300) = 1704m. (Note: Key 'a' 2304 suggests cumulative corrections applied in specific texts).

q: 56. If aerodrome reference temperature is 17°C, the net designed length of the runway
explain: Temperature correction is applied after elevation correction to account for air density changes at the site.

q: 57. Standard sea-level temperature is 15°C; temperature gradient equals
explain: The answer key specifies 15°C, though the physical standard lapse rate is 6.5°C per 1000m.

q: 58. *The basic length of runway is 600m and RL of the airport is 100m. Actual length of the runway is
59. In question number 58, if temperature at the site is 20°C, then runway length is
explain: Applying the temperature correction (1% per 1°C rise above standard) to the elevation-corrected length results in ~645m.

q: 60. The standard length of the runway is 3000 m. If RL of the airport is 600 m, the design length of the runway is
61. Total correction for elevation and temperature should not be more than
explain: ICAO guidelines state that the combined correction for altitude and temperature should not exceed 35% of basic length.

q: 62. The maximum difference in elevation divided by total length of runway is
explain: Effective gradient is calculated as the ratio of the maximum elevation difference to the total runway length.

q: 63. Effective gradient for the diagram [RL 101 -- RL 99 -- RL 100] is
explain: Based on the elevation profile provided in the image, the gradient calculates to 1 in 6.

q: 64. The purpose of apron in aircraft is
explain: The apron is the area where aircraft are parked, unloaded or loaded, refueled, or boarded.

q: 65. Apron is used for loading and unloading of passenger while taxiway is
explain: Taxiways are defined paths on an airport connecting runways with aprons and other facilities for taxiing aircraft.

q: 66. *Flight time refers to
explain: Often called 'block-to-block' time, it starts when an aircraft first moves for takeoff and ends when it stops at the destination gate.

q: 67. *The height of the pilot's eye above runway surface is assumed
explain: For design purposes, specifically sight distance and gradient changes, the pilot's eye height is assumed to be 3m.

q: 68. *Runway orientation is made so that landing and take off are
explain: Operating against the wind (headwind) provides more lift during takeoff and better braking during landing.

q: 69. *Strength of runway pavement is expressed as
explain: California Bearing Ratio (CBR) is the standard empirical test used to estimate the load-bearing capacity of pavement subgrades.

q: 70. Beaufort scale used for measuring wind strength has numerals
explain: The scale typically ranges from 0 (Calm) to 12 (Hurricane force).

q: 71. Two single runway may be arranged so as to have
explain: Runway configurations are chosen based on prevailing winds and can take various intersecting or non-intersecting shapes.

q: 72. The I.C.A.O. has two governing bodies named
explain: The ICAO is composed of an Assembly (all member states) and a Council (elected executive body).

q: 73. According to I.C.A.O. all markings on runways are painted
explain: Runway markings are mandatory white to ensure high contrast against the asphalt or concrete surface.

q: 74. The marking of taxiway is yellow while on apron is
explain: Yellow markings are used for all movement areas other than runways, including taxiways and aprons.

q: 75. The colour of wind direction indicator is
explain: Wind indicators (windsocks) must be in high-visibility colors; ICAO allows several of these combinations.

q: 76. The threshold markings are
options: placed symmetrically on either side of the runway centre line
explain: Threshold markings consist of a pattern of longitudinal stripes of uniform dimensions disposed symmetrically about the centerline of a runway.

q: 77. *For night landing, the thresholds are lighted
explain: Threshold lights are fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach to the runway.

q: 78. The bearing of the runway at threshold is 290°, the runway number is
explain: Runway numbers are determined by dividing the magnetic bearing by 10 and rounding to the nearest whole number (290/10 = 29).

q: 79. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: F.I.R. stands for flight information regions
F.I.C stands for flight information centre
explain: All provided definitions for Flight Information Regions, Centres, and standard radii for control areas/zones are correct in aviation standards.

q: 80. If the visibility of environment is less than 4 KNm then pilot must follow
explain: When visibility falls below the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) limit, pilots must switch to Instrument Flight Rules (IFR).

q: 81. The best direction of a runway is along the direction of
options: longest line on wind rose diagram
shortest line on wind rose diagram
line clear of wind rose diagram
explain: To maximize wind coverage, the runway is oriented along the direction of the prevailing winds (the longest line on a wind rose).

q: 82. The coordinates of the ends of a runway are (5000, 5000) and (8000, 7000). The co-ordinates of the A.R.P are
explain: The Airport Reference Point (ARP) is the geometric center. Calculation: (5000+8000)/2 = 6500 and (5000+7000)/2 = 6000.

q: 83. The bearing of the longest line of a wind rose is S 45° E. The bearing of the runway will be numbered
explain: S 45° E is 135°. The opposite end is 315°. Runway numbers are 135/10 ≈ 13 and 315/10 ≈ 31.

q: 84. The WCB of the 1st and 2nd end of the runway are 80° and 260° respectively. Find the runway number indicated on the 1st end
explain: The runway number for the 1st end is 80/10 = 8.

q: 85. *The bearing of the 1st end of straight runway is 90°. Find the runway number of 1st end
explain: The runway number is 90/10 = 9.

q: 86. The airplane of IAR was hijacked from Tribhuvan International Airport in
explain: Indian Airlines flight IC 814 was hijacked on Dec 24, 1999, after taking off from Kathmandu.

q: 87. The maximum number of airports is located in the district
explain: Solukhumbu district has the highest number of airports in Nepal including Lukla and Phaplu.

q: 88. Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal was established in
explain: CAAN was established as an autonomous body on Dec 31, 1998.

q: 89. The number of international airports in Nepal
explain: Nepal recognizes 4 international airports: TIA, GBIA, Pokhara, and Nijgadh (under project).

q: 90. *The width of taxiway is kept about
explain: Generally, the width of the taxiway is kept roughly 1/2 of the runway width.

q: 91. The purposed international airport in Nepal is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport in Bara is the major proposed international airport.

q: 92. The National pride project concerned with airport is
explain: Nijgadh International Airport is a designated National Pride Project of Nepal.

q: 93. Lord Ram returned from Lanka to Ayodhya through
explain: According to Hindu mythology, the Pushpak Viman was used by Lord Ram.

q: 94. A flexible pavement of runway consists of
options: finishing coarse, surface course and base course
surface course, base course and sub-base course
base course, sub-base course and rough course
explain: Flexible pavements consist of the surface course, base course, and sub-base course over the subgrade.

q: 95. As the elevation of airport increases the runway length
explain: Higher elevation means thinner air, which reduces lift, requiring a longer runway for takeoff.

q: 96. *As the temperature of airport increases the runway length
explain: Higher temperature decreases air density, requiring a longer runway length to generate lift.

q: 97. As the elevation & temperature of airport increases the density of air
explain: Both increasing altitude and increasing temperature lead to lower air density.

q: 98. Nose hanger is used normally for accommodation of ............size aircraft.
explain: Nose hangars are designed to fit the front portion of various aircraft sizes for maintenance.

q: 99. *Holding line marking is provided in
explain: Holding lines are marked on taxiways where aircraft must stop before entering a runway.

q: 100. The landing and take off of an aircraft is made against the direction of wind. In no case the centre line of the runway should make angle with the wind direction exceeding
explain: The runway is oriented to minimize crosswind; a 40-degree angle is a common limit for orientation calculation.

q: 101. Runway dimension of TIA after extension held in 2020 AD is
explain: The runway was extended to 3350 meters to accommodate larger wide-body aircraft.

q: 102. Runway surface strength of TIA is
explain: This refers to the Pavement Classification Number (PCN) value for the TIA runway.

q: 103. *ACN refers to
explain: ACN (Aircraft Classification Number) expresses the relative effect of an aircraft on a pavement.

q: 104. LCN refers to
explain: LCN is a system used to classify the bearing strength of pavements and aircraft loads.

q: 105. Normally fuel provided in aircraft having piston engine is
explain: Piston-engine aircraft typically use aviation gasoline (Avgas).

q: 106. The runway of Tribhuvan International Airport is one way where landing occurs
explain: Due to northern terrain, landing at TIA primarily occurs from the South (Runway 02).

q: 107. The old name of TIA was
explain: It was originally known as Gauchar Airport before being renamed Tribhuvan International Airport.

q: 108. *Heliport is used for
explain: A heliport is an area designated for landing, takeoff, maintenance, and storage of helicopters.

q: 109. The roof of hanger is made of
explain: Large hangar spans are typically achieved using steel frames with GI sheet roofing.

q: 110. The types of hanger used for parking of large size aircraft is called
explain: Nose hangars provide shelter for the forward section of large aircraft for maintenance.

q: 111. What is the function of aircraft drainage?
options: to lower the sub-surface water level
to intercept & divert the surface and ground water flow
explain: Drainage systems handle surface runoff and sub-surface water to protect the pavement structure.

q: 112. *As per ICAO for determining basic runway length aircraft should come to stop within
explain: ICAO standards specify that aircraft should be able to stop within 60% of the effective runway length.

q: 113. The shape of landing direction indicator
explain: A 'Landing T' is the standard shape used to show the landing direction at airports.

q: 114. The no. of traverse rows of light in approach lighting near the threshold (As per Calvert & ICAO) is
explain: The Calvert approach lighting system uses a specific configuration of traverse rows.

q: 115. *The angle between the longitudinal axis of the fuselage and the horizontal axis is called
explain: Rotation around the lateral axis (nose up/down) is known as the pitch angle.

q: 116. The angle between the longitudinal axis of fuselage and an inclined plane below which the views of the pilots are blocked by some part of the aircraft is known as
explain: The cockpit cutoff angle defines the pilot's visual limit over the nose of the aircraft.

q: 117. The angle formed by the longitudinal axis of the fuselage and the direction of movement of nose gear
explain: This refers to the castor angle in the landing gear steering geometry.

q: 118. *Aircraft facilities found in aircraft are
explain: All these facilities are standard components within modern aircraft for safety and environment control.

q: 119. *Annex 14 published by ICAO contains
explain: Annex 14 (Aerodromes) contains specifications for airport design, construction, and operations.

q: 120. *In the premix asphalt concrete of airport pavement construction aggregate is also heated to
explain: Heating ensures moisture removal and better adhesion of asphalt to the aggregate.

q: 121. *The CBR method is used to design
explain: The California Bearing Ratio (CBR) method is a standard empirical approach for flexible pavement design.

q: 122. *Runway is designed on the basis of
explain: Design loads and geometry for runways are heavily influenced by aircraft gear configuration (nose gear/main gear).

q: 123. *Runway of airport is designed by
explain: Runway design accounts for static aircraft weight, axle loads, and dynamic impact loads.

q: 124. The metrological condition which influences the size and location of an airport is
explain: Meteorological factors like wind direction and pressure (altitude) determine orientation and runway length.

q: 125. The depressions and undulations in the pavement of runway are caused due to
explain: All these factors contribute to the structural failure and deformation of runway pavements.

q: 126. *Which of the following international association is the one that represent an authority for aviation?
explain: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) is the global regulatory authority.

q: 127. *Taxiway is located in between the
explain: Taxiways serve as the link for aircraft moving between the runway and the apron/terminal areas.

q: 128. *Holding aprons, run up pads or holding bags are placed adjacent to the ends of runways for
options: storage of aircraft prior to take off
use as a space to let bypass another aircraft
explain: These areas allow for engine checks and sequencing without obstructing taxiway traffic.

q: 129. *Classification of Airport by ICAO is based on
explain: ICAO airport classification uses a code based on both runway length and aircraft dimensions.

q: 130. *In the premix asphalt concrete of airport pavement construction aggregate is also heated to
explain: Heating aggregates is essential to remove moisture and ensure a quality homogeneous mix.

q: 131. *The runway length of Tribhuvan International Airport is
explain: The TIA runway length of 3350 meters is approximately 10,990 feet.

q: 132. *The enclosure/structure where an aircraft is kept for maintenance and repair is known as
explain: A hangar is the specific building structure designed for aircraft storage and maintenance.

q: 133. *Aprons are serviced as:
options: to connect the terminal building with paved runway
explain: Aprons are intended for activities like loading/unloading cargo, fueling, and parking.

q: 134. *In a very-density- airports, characteristics load per landing gear in KN is :
explain: High-density airports are designed for heavier landing gear loads, typically around 700 KN.

q: 135. *The capacity of an airport depends upon:
options: maximum acceptable delay for departing aircraft
explain: Airport capacity is determined by both physical infrastructure (taxiways) and operational delays.

q: 136. *As per ICAO recommendation minimum width of safety area for instrumental runway should is:
explain: For instrument runways, ICAO recommends a minimum safety area width of 300 meters.

q: 137. *For A,B and C types of airports, longitudinal gradient of the runway recommended by ICAO is :
explain: ICAO recommends a maximum longitudinal gradient of 1.5% for major airport categories (A, B, C).

q: 138. *In FY 2072/73, various accidents were occured and there was a heavy losses of lives in Nepal. Among the various airports which of the following is most dangerous in Nepal.
explain: Tenzing-Hillary (Lukla) Airport is considered one of the most dangerous due to terrain and short runway.

q: 139. *Windrose diagram of Tribhuvan International Airport indicates that the runway is oriented as
explain: TIA's runway is oriented roughly North-South, designated as 02 and 20.

q: 140. *A domestic airport is an airport that handles only
explain: Domestic airports serve only internal flights within the same country.

q: 141. *I.C.A.O has classifies
explain: ICAO provides classification standards for runway geometry, length, and pavement strength.

q: 142. Which one airpot come in operation from 2022 AD ?
explain: Gautam Buddha International Airport (GBIA) officially began international operations in May 2022.
